ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Now, conveyor belts for transporting goods are widely used in stations, factories, workshops, and docks. As shown in the figure, it is a schematic diagram of a horizontal conveyor belt device. The taut conveyor belt AB always operates at a constant speed of $v=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. An object with a mass of $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is placed at point $A$ with no initial velocity. The sliding friction force exerted by the conveyor belt on the object causes it to start moving with uniformly accelerated linear motion, and then the object moves with uniform linear motion at the same speed as the conveyor belt. Let the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the conveyor belt be $\mu=0.2$, the distance between $A$ and $B$ be $L=4\mathrm{m}$, and $g$ be $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the magnitude of the acceleration when the object just starts to move?
2. What is the time taken for an object to travel from $A$ to $B$?
3. If the operating speed of the conveyor belt is increased, can the object be transported to point $B$ more quickly? What is the shortest time required to transport the object from point $A$ to point $B$, and what is the corresponding minimum operating speed of the conveyor belt?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal conveyor belt; the upper straight segment extends from the left end A to the right end B; the block is placed on the upper surface near the left end A; above the conveyor belt there is a rightward arrow labeled v, indicating that the upper segment of the conveyor belt moves in the direction of B. Then reason: When the block has just been placed on it, it slides leftward relative to the conveyor belt, so the kinetic friction force exerted by the conveyor belt on the block is rightward. In the horizontal direction there is only kinetic friction, with magnitude f=μmg, so the acceleration a=f/m=μg=0.2×10=2 m/s^2. When the conveyor belt speed v=2 m/s, the time needed for the block to accelerate from rest to the same speed as the conveyor belt is t1=v/a=2/2=1 s. During this time the distance the block advances is s1=v^2/(2a)=2^2/(2×2)=1 m. Because s1=1 m<L=4 m, afterwards the block moves at a uniform speed of 2 m/s through the remaining distance 4-1=3 m, and the required time is t2=3/2=1.5 s. The total time T=t1+t2=1+1.5=2.5 s. If the conveyor belt speed is changed to a general U, the acceleration is still determined by kinetic friction, a=2 m/s^2. If the block can accelerate to U before reaching B, then the total time is T=U/a+(L-U^2/(2a))/U=L/U+U/(2a), with applicable condition U^2/(2a)≤L, that is U≤sqrt(2aL)=4 m/s. This expression reaches the boundary minimum value at U=4 m/s: T=4/4+4/(2×2)=1+1=2 s. If U>4 m/s, before the block reaches B it still has not caught up with the conveyor belt, and only keeps advancing with acceleration a, with time T=sqrt(2L/a)=sqrt(2×4/2)=2 s. Therefore increasing the conveyor belt speed can be faster than the original 2.5 s, but the shortest time can only be 2 s; the minimum conveyor belt speed needed to reach this shortest time is 4 m/s.
